name: DCASE2020 Challenge Task 3 (Sound Event Localization and Detection)
ability_definition: The ability to tell the direction from which a sound originated.

task_realism.reasoning: The core task is estimating the direction of arrival of sound events in reverberant rooms, and this is exactly what the ability asks for. The TAU-NIGENS 2020 data uses real spatial room impulse responses and recorded ambient noise, and it includes moving sources. However, the scenes are synthetically mixed from isolated clips of 14 predefined classes, with at most two overlapping sources. Real workplace localization, such as finding a machine fault, reacting to alarms or tracking an approaching vehicle, involves open-ended sounds and messier scenes.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation is offline on pre-recorded clips from a fixed microphone array. The environment has controlled room variety, bounded polyphony and no directional interferers (those were added only in 2021). There is no active listening, head or body movement, real-time demand, or consequence for errors. Reverberation, noise and source motion do add meaningful difficulty. Still, the distribution is narrower and cleaner than real acoustic workplaces.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The benchmark measures azimuth and elevation angular error and localization recall, which covers the directional core of the ability. Coverage is narrowed in three ways. The localization metrics are class-dependent, so a direction only counts when the sound type is also correct. Distance and near/far judgments are excluded. Performance on unfamiliar sounds outside the 14 classes and in dense multi-source scenes is untested.

format_match.reasoning: The input is 4-channel first-order Ambisonics or tetrahedral array audio, and the output is frame-wise DOA coordinates. That is a natural format for machine acoustic scene analysis, but not for the human binaural perception the O*NET ability describes. In real work, the result of localizing a sound is orienting toward it, pointing or describing its location, not emitting angle trajectories.

transferability_reasoning: DCASE2020 SELD directly tests direction-of-arrival estimation under reverberation, noise and moving sources, so it targets the right construct better than most audio benchmarks. Its transfer is limited by synthetic mixing, a closed set of 14 classes, bounded polyphony and class-coupled localization metrics. The fixed-array, offline format also differs from how humans localize sounds in real workplaces.

2021.model_or_system: USTC'20 (USTC team, ResNet-Conformer ensemble with four-stage data augmentation; top-ranked DCASE2020 Task 3 system)
2021.metric: Location-dependent F-score F≤20° (%), on the DCASE2020 Task 3 evaluation set
2021.human_reference: General adult population with normal hearing, the typical person who judges sound direction in everyday and work settings. This comparison assumes a hypothetical listener hearing the scenes binaurally.
